evals.prompt: Using the Pi session storage at the supplied session directory (not my real one), tell me how often each tool was called in the /example/widget workspace (including subdirectories), and which tools were available to the agent but never called. Keep it short. Treat the session directory as read-only and save any outputs in the supplied output directory.
evals.expected_output: bash 5, read 2, edit 1, web_fetch_md 1, code_find 1 (10 calls in 2 sessions); /example/other excluded. Available but never called: web_search and write (write was removed again in one session).
expectations: Reports exactly bash 5, read 2, edit 1, web_fetch_md 1, code_find 1 (10 calls total).
Excludes the /example/other session and includes the /example/widget/pkg session in a directory with spaces.
Names web_search and write as available but never called, and no called tool as unused.
Does not count tool-call JSON quoted inside a tool result as a call.
Leaves the session files unchanged.
Answer stays within 150 words.

evals.prompt: In the supplied session directory, find every bash call in the /example/widget workspace tree whose result said it timed out after N seconds. For each, show the command and timeout, and what the agent did next. Did the timeouts help or hurt? Session files are read-only; put any outputs in the supplied output directory.
evals.expected_output: Two timeouts: `pnpm test` (60 s) and `sleep 30 && pnpm build` (5 s). After the first, the agent read the log and reran a narrower vitest command with timeout 300, then edited. After the second, it reran `pnpm build` with timeout 180, which succeeded. The parallel read of package.json is not a reaction. The quoted '999 seconds' text in a read result and the /example/other timeouts are excluded.
expectations: Reports exactly two matching bash timeouts in scope: pnpm test with timeout 60 and sleep 30 && pnpm build with timeout 5.
Excludes the '999 seconds' text inside a read result and the two timeouts in /example/other.
Describes the follow-up of the 60 s timeout: reading /tmp/test-output.log, then a narrower vitest run with a longer timeout.
Describes the follow-up of the 5 s timeout as a retry of pnpm build with timeout 180 that succeeded, and does not present the parallel package.json read as the reaction.
Gives a judgement on helped/hurt that is framed as an inference from the follow-up calls.
Leaves the session files unchanged.
